subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (Acme POC)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (Acme POC)

Hi Dana — great to meet you and the Acme team today. Quick recap and my recommended next steps from the demo + initial evals.

1) Summary of what we heard from Acme
- Primary goal: deploy an in-product summarization assistant for operations runbooks with tight hallucination constraints.
- Target traffic: ~100k tokens/day during pilot, expected to scale.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 500ms for single-turn queries; cost sensitivity for token unit economics.

2) Shortlist (recommended models) + rationale
- redwood-instruct-7b-q4: Best latency/cost balance for deterministic summarization workflows. Strong at instruction-following and relatively low token cost when quantized. Good candidate for canary and rapid iteration.
- mistral-instruct-7b (8bit tuned): Higher quality on longer-context summarization and fewer factual errors in our evals, modestly slower but still within your 95p target for expected payload sizes.
- llama2-13b-8bit (conservative mode): Highest quality on edge cases we saw in your sample prompts, but materially higher cost and 95p latency risk without aggressive batching or dedicated capacity.

Tradeoffs (cost / latency / quality):
- redwood-instruct-7b-q4: Low cost, low latency, slightly higher false positive hallucinations on rare, domain-specific snippets.
- mistral-instruct-7b: Medium cost, medium latency, best balance for recall/precision on runbook-style inputs.
- llama2-13b-8bit: High cost, highest quality on tricky long-context threads; consider only if accuracy ramp is critical and budget allows.

3) Evaluation assets attached
- acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts & ground-truths you shared)
- benchmark_summary_acme.md (links to run outputs and metrics)
- latency_cost_estimate_ACME.xlsx (rough cost + p95 latency estimates for the pilot)

4) Proposed next steps
- Confirm which two models you want us to run a 48–72h targeted eval on (we recommend redwood-instruct-7b-q4 + mistral-instruct-7b).
- We’ll run evals on your prompt set and return per-prompt quality metrics (ROUGE/EM + hallucination flag) and token-cost estimates.
- If agreed, schedule a short canary plan for a 2-week pilot with fallback rules and basic monitoring.

Please confirm if the above shortlist aligns with your priorities (quality-first vs cost-first). Happy to jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow to lock the eval window.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, benchmark_summary_acme.md, latency_cost_estimate_ACME.xlsx

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmecorp.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (Acme POC)

Thanks Sean — useful summary. A few clarifying questions before we pick the two to evaluate:

- Hallucination: can you share how you measured hallucination in the attached benchmark? We need near-zero hallucinations on safety-critical sections of our runbooks.
- Cost target: our internal threshold for pilot is <$0.0009 per token on average. Do any of the recommended models meet that at our expected volume?
- Latency: the 95p <= 500ms target is strict for our UI. Can caching or prefix-KV help for repeated queries?
- Compliance: please include the SOC 2 brief / how logs are retained — our security team will ask.

Also, Bill Park (ops@acmecorp.com) asked if you can run the evals on a subset of the dataset that is flagged as "safety-critical" first.

If you can share quick answers (and updated cost table if needed) we’ll confirm the two models for the run.

—Dana
Dana Liu
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme Corp
Dana.Liu@acmecorp.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmecorp.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (Acme POC)

Thanks for the quick follow-up, Dana — a few quick points while we schedule the targeted eval: 

- Hallucination measurement: we use a mixed methodology — automated detectors + human annotation on a stratified sample. For the pilot we’ll run a focused "safety-critical" evaluation first (the subset Bill requested) and report per-example hallucination flags and rationale.
- Cost: see attached sheet for ballpark per-token numbers at pilot scale (estimates based on 100k tokens/day, with and without KV caching). We’ll update if you change the expected volume.
- Latency: prefix/KV caching for repeated runbook snippets can reduce end-to-end latency significantly; our runtime supports per-route caching and bypass for freshness-critical queries.
- Compliance: Sean, can you attach the SOC 2 one-pager + retention policy doc in the next message so Dana can loop in security.

Action items:
- Dana: confirm the two models to run (we recommend redwood-instruct-7b-q4 + mistral-instruct-7b).
- Priyom: can you provide an estimated cost/95p-latency table for 100k tokens/day, 2k context, with dedicated capacity vs shared hosted?

Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist + tradeoffs (Acme POC)

Forwarding quick engineering estimates based on the prompt set and traffic window we discussed. These are conservative numbers for planning; we can run a short pilot to validate.

Summary (100k tokens/day, median prompt length ~180 tokens, context 2k):
- Option A: Hosted shared capacity, redwood-instruct-7b-q4
  - Estimated avg cost/token: ~$0.00065
  - Expected p95 latency: ~320–420ms (depends on burst and multi-tenant queuing)
  - Notes: Lowest entry cost, immediate onboarding.

- Option B: Hosted shared capacity, mistral-instruct-7b (8bit)
  - Estimated avg cost/token: ~$0.00095
  - Expected p95 latency: ~420–560ms
  - Notes: Better quality, may exceed your $0.0009 threshold at this scale but within range if we enable KV caching.

- Option C: Dedicated capacity (1 reserved instance), llama2-13b-8bit
  - Estimated avg cost/token: ~$0.0018 (amortized over pilot commit)
  - Expected p95 latency: ~380–480ms
  - Notes: Highest quality and predictable latency; requires a commit for dedicated pool pricing to make sense.

Caching impact: prefix/KV caching can reduce token emission by ~12–35% depending on repetition in your dataset — simple caching assumptions in the attached spreadsheet show cost improvements that could bring mistral-instruct-7b under your cost target for many traffic profiles.

Attachments: latency_cost_estimate_ACME.xlsx (tabbed breakdown: per-model cost, p95 latency buckets, caching scenarios).

Next steps I recommend:
- Approve the two models for 48–72h targeted eval (we'll run on the safety-critical subset first).
- We’ll deliver: per-example hallucination flags, quality metrics, cost projection table, and a short canary plan template.

Happy to hop on a call early next week to walk through the spreadsheet with your ops/security leads.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
